simple.meaning: בֵּית בָּרָה (Bêyth Bârâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “Beth-Barah , a place in Palestine.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: בֵּית בָּרָה (H1012) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Judges 7:24, with occurrences in Judges.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בֵּית בָּרָה (H1012) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in בֵּית בָּרָה (H1012) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: בֵּית בָּרָה (Bêyth Bârâh) / H1012 is traced through Judges 7:24 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H1012. Beth Barah בָּרָה בֵּית proper name, of a location in combin . וְאֶתהַֿיַּרְדֵּן בּ ׳עַד ׳בּ Judg 7:24 (twice in verse) (? = עֲבָרָה בֵּית place of ford ).
definitions.rootNote: probably from 1004 and 5679 ; house of (the) ford;

occurrences.englishText: Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, “Come down against Midian and take the waters before them as far as Beth Barah, even the Jordan!” So all the men of Ephraim were gathered together and took the waters as far as Beth Barah, even the Jordan.
